high_1_whole_tree_reparse.change: Test-OwnedPreviewTreeSafe replaced by an explicit System.Collections.Stack walk of the whole tree with no depth bound: every directory is listed non-recursively (Get-ChildItem without -Recurse, which lists a reparse point instead of descending through it, also on Windows PowerShell 5.1), each entry's Attributes are tested for ReparsePoint before the entry is used as a path, and no link is ever followed. Any reparse point anywhere in the tree refuses as stage 'reparse'; an enumeration error refuses as 'tree-read'; more entries than the single explicit limit (Get-PreviewTreeElementLimit = 10000) refuses as 'size'. In every refusal nothing is deleted.
high_1_whole_tree_reparse.reproduction: deep-junction-delta-probe.ps1 raw exit 0: the copied previous depth-3 algorithm returns old_depth_bounded_walk_safe=True for a junction at root/data/a/b/link, the new walk returns safe=False reason=reparse counted=8, and the external sentinel was intact after the case removal

high_2_native_credential_readback.change: The second cmdkey /delete heuristic is gone. The exact delete stays a direct cmdkey.exe invocation with an argument list (never a shell); absence is then proven only by a minimal Add-Type P/Invoke advapi32!CredReadW(target, CRED_TYPE_GENERIC=1, 0) with CredFree on success. Success (credential still exists) refuses as stage 'absence', GetLastError 1168 ERROR_NOT_FOUND is the only accepted absence ('verified'), any other code refuses as 'absence-error'; the credential blob and user name are never read or printed. A test-only script-scope seam (PreviewCredentialReadbackSeam) substitutes only the readback verdict for the safety suite; production never sets it, and an unset seam always uses the real readback.
high_2_native_credential_readback.native_probe: credread-probe.ps1 raw exit 0: add_type_compiled=True absent_code=1168 add_exit=0 present_code=0 delete_exit=0 after_delete_code=1168

focused_fix.suite_self_cleanup: The suite drops its own junction links with [System.IO.Directory]::Delete($link, $false) instead of Remove-Item -Force, because a non-interactive PowerShell host cannot answer the junction confirmation prompt; junction-delete-probe.ps1 (raw exit 0) shows that this call removes only the link, that Remove-Item -Recurse -Force on a directory containing a junction does not follow it, and that Remove-Item -Force without -Recurse fails on a junction in a non-interactive host.
